research_mode: official Home Office primary statistical guidance only; stop-search developing fields, arrests and mental-health detention methodology gates; no parcel result or local-risk score claimed

sources.name: Use-of-force incident definition
verified_claims: Use of force includes restraint tactics and equipment such as handcuffs, batons or TASER during an encounter.
limitations: The field records whether a force tactic was reported, not whether it was lawful, necessary or proportionate.

sources.name: Use-of-force partial coverage
verified_claims: Thirty-nine of 44 forces supplied stop-and-search use-of-force information for the year ending March 2025, covering 92.4% of searches.
limitations: The reported proportion is not complete national coverage and must not be assigned to missing forces.

sources.name: Cross-system force-linkage limitation
verified_claims: Force comparisons can reflect differences in recording standards and the ability to link stop-and-search records with use-of-force systems.
limitations: A low linked rate may reflect system linkage rather than lower operational use of force.

sources.name: Clothing-removal categories
verified_claims: The collection distinguishes no clothing removed, outer clothing only, more than outer clothing, and full strip search exposing intimate parts.
limitations: Some force systems cannot distinguish the first two categories.

sources.name: Combined clothing category rule
verified_claims: The bulletin groups no-clothing and outer-clothing-only searches where six forces could not distinguish them.
limitations: The combined category cannot support separate force-level estimates for its components.

sources.name: Voluntary full-strip location data
verified_claims: Full-strip-search location was a new voluntary field supplied by 12 forces for the year ending March 2025.
limitations: The resulting distribution is not representative of all forces or all full strip searches.

sources.name: Voluntary supervisor-consultation data
verified_claims: Whether a supervisor was consulted for a full strip search was voluntarily supplied by 12 forces and was incomplete within those records.
limitations: Missing consultation information must not be treated as evidence that consultation did not occur.

sources.name: Appropriate-adult data boundary
verified_claims: Only 13 relevant forces supplied information on appropriate-adult presence for full strip searches of children.
limitations: The published proportion must not be generalized to forces or cases without data.

sources.name: Hotspot-map scale boundary
verified_claims: Hotspot-map scales differ by police force area and are designed for within-area highlighting, not direct comparison between areas.
limitations: Map colours or intensity must not be compared across police force maps as a common scale.

sources.name: Transient-population hotspot context
verified_claims: Some high-activity LSOAs contain stations, shopping centres, tourism or protest locations with populations far above resident counts.
limitations: Resident-population denominators alone can misrepresent exposure and do not produce parcel-level risk.

sources.name: Arrest offence-group comparability break
verified_claims: Reason-for-arrest data from the year ending March 2016 uses amended ONS offence groups and is not directly comparable with earlier years.
limitations: Long-run trends crossing the classification change require a harmonized series.

sources.name: Arrest-person versus offence-unit boundary
verified_claims: Arrest statistics count persons or arrest events, while police recorded crime counts offences; one offence can generate several arrests.
limitations: Arrest counts and offence counts must not be compared as if they share the same statistical unit.

sources.name: Unknown arrest-offence classification
verified_claims: Derbyshire reported 1,062 arrests with unknown offence group because manual classification was considered potentially inaccurate.
limitations: Unknown arrests must be excluded or retained as unknown rather than redistributed across offence groups.

sources.name: Arrest age-analysis exclusions
verified_claims: Age analyses exclude unknown ages, the single arrest aged nine or under, and arrests with unknown offence group where specified.
limitations: Published age distributions are conditional on included records, not all arrests.

sources.name: Metropolitan Police SDE system-change effect
verified_claims: A Metropolitan Police data-system change materially increased missing self-defined ethnicity in arrest records.
limitations: Changes in the missing category must not be interpreted as demographic change.

sources.name: Arrest observed-ethnicity boundary
verified_claims: Officer-observed ethnicity has higher completion but lacks a Mixed category and is not equivalent to self-defined ethnicity.
limitations: Observed and self-defined measures must not be merged without an explicit methodology.

sources.name: Mental-health place-of-safety comparability break
verified_claims: Revised guidance for recording accident-and-emergency settings means place-of-safety data from the year ending March 2024 is not fully comparable with earlier years.
limitations: A time-series break must be preserved in trend analysis.

sources.name: Police and NHS mental-health source boundary
verified_claims: NHS inpatient detention data includes many cases without police involvement and can differ from police or NPCC place-of-safety data because sources differ.
limitations: Counts from the separate systems must not be treated as interchangeable.

sources.name: Section 135 collection scope
verified_claims: Section 135 incidents are counted only where an officer uses warrant powers to enter premises and/or remove the person to a place of safety.
limitations: Police attendance without exercising either warrant power is outside this dataset.

sources.name: Section 135 incomplete-series boundary
verified_claims: Section 135 analysis uses data from 34 of 43 territorial forces and is designated Official Statistics in development.
limitations: It provides an indication only and cannot support complete national or parcel-level inference.
